title: Cat50: Temporal Win-Sequence Encoding
summary: Encode the ORDER of last-10-game outcomes as features — not just rolling averages. A team that lost early then won recently (improving trajectory) is fundamentally different from a team winning early and now declining, even at identical aggregate win%. Rolling averages lose this directional information.

research_basis.finding: Temporal sequence models outperform tabular rolling averages for NBA prediction; MC-dropout LSTM achieves Brier 0.199 vs XGBoost 0.202 with equal features
LSTM sequence encoding of game outcomes captures non-stationary momentum patterns undetectable by window averages
500+ features include sequence pattern indicators, not just window statistics

expected_mechanism: GA will discover that seq50_slope_diff (momentum trajectory difference) is a superior predictor vs raw h_wp10 / a_wp10 for teams in transitional states (post-injury return, coaching change, hot/cold streaks)
validation_plan: Monitor next 5 cycles — check if seq50_* features appear in any island's selected feature set. If seq50_slope_diff appears in top-50 features of any island, proposal is confirmed useful.

cross_project_applicability.political: Political event sequences (EO → vote → enforcement) could benefit from same ordered encoding. Proposed as Cat26 for future cycle.
